aiBrReviews.statement: In Standard Message Data Segment (Data Segment No. 100), field 14 (Sequence Number) is required and must be present.
aiBrReviews.reason: The Segment 100 field table marks Element 86 required. Seven linked negative cases deliberately omit the Standard Segment value; six other cases exercise a Sequence Number field, including four Segment 100 and two Segment 109 cases. Segment 109 observations do not prove the narrower Segment 100 claim.
aiBrReviews.chainAssessment: The linked cases provide omission/positive design evidence. Producer-declared response code 1 for omission is not independently validated. At least one omitted-100 case also carries Sequence Number values in Segments 119/132; those do not satisfy the Segment 100 requirement.
aiBrReviews.testBrScope: SEG100-R-019 additionally claims six digits and lifecycle persistence; SEG100-R-037 adds follow-up and approval context; BR-SEG100-E86-001 is a draft format-only authored rule. No independently approved presence-only Test rule was established.
openIssues: Review all 13 cases and approved/candidate record conflicts.
Do not count non-100 Sequence Number fields as coverage of the Segment 100 BR.

aiBrReviews.statement: Sequence Number: Fixed length six-digit numeric field identifying a transaction for its lifetime.
aiBrReviews.reason: The statement follows the source Element 86 definition. Six linked cases use 000001; four locate it in Segment 100 and two in Segment 109. The producer anchor proposes several segments, while SEG100-R-019 is Segment 100 scoped and SEG109-R-015 is Segment 109 scoped.
aiBrReviews.chainAssessment: No lower/upper boundary, zero, length, or nonnumeric mutation appears in this six-case set. Independent case records do not compare a sequence across the transaction lifetime.
aiBrReviews.testBrScope: SEG100-R-019 and SEG118-R-008 include lifecycle language in different segments; SEG109-R-015 states required six numeric characters but not lifetime persistence. Authored BR-SEG100-E86-001 adds a six-digit positive and five-digit negative design. All remain review-required.
openIssues: Add valid range boundaries and invalid-range cases.
Do not infer lifetime identity from repeated standalone values.

aiBrReviews.statement: Sequence Number must persist in all subsequent transactions associated with the initial authorization request.
aiBrReviews.reason: The statement closely tracks the source Element 86 purpose. The six linked AI cases are individual records; four use Segment 100 and two Segment 109, all with the same literal value, but no case links an initial authorization to follow-up messages.
aiBrReviews.chainAssessment: Repeated 000001 values across independent cases do not demonstrate persistence. Authored independent Test chains exist for authorization completion, authorization void, sale void and timeout TOR with same-sequence and mismatch fixtures. Their data readiness remains REVIEW_REQUIRED and none was executed.
aiBrReviews.testBrScope: The authored lifecycle chains strengthen the Test-side comparison and are retained by reference. SEG100-R-037 also claims approval context, whose source applicability remains unresolved.
openIssues: AI chain has no initial/follow-up linked transaction assertion.
Test fixture readiness remains REVIEW_REQUIRED; PASS/FAIL fields are not execution evidence.
Review the separate approval-context obligation before treating SEG100-R-037 as fully aligned.
